description: Integrate the Next.js frontend with the new FastAPI backend behind a BACKEND_URL env flag, with graceful fallback to the current live-fetch behavior when BACKEND_URL is unset OR the backend is unreachable, so the deployed Vercel prototype never breaks. Update root .env.example with the new env vars, and write the backend README/docs (local dev, backfill, prod deploy for Neo4j Aura + Qdrant Cloud + Railway/Render/Fly.io). Do NOT touch the 3D engine (Step 2). Depends on FEAT-003 for the API contract.
steps: Create lib/backend-client.ts: a tiny typed client that reads process.env.BACKEND_URL. Export isBackendEnabled() (true iff BACKEND_URL set) and fetchGraphFromBackend(params) / fetchArticleFromBackend(id) using fetch with a short timeout (AbortController, ~4s) and returning null on any error so callers can fall back. Never throw to the caller.

Modify app/api/graph/route.ts: at the top of GET, if isBackendEnabled(), try fetchGraphFromBackend with the same category/startDate/endDate params; if it returns a non-empty graph, return it (preserving the existing response shape and no-store headers). On null/empty/error, fall through to the EXISTING live-fetch-first -> /tmp -> mock logic entirely unchanged. Keep all current behavior intact when BACKEND_URL is unset.

Modify app/api/news/route.ts similarly where sensible: if isBackendEnabled(), attempt to source articles from the backend (e.g. a backend articles/list endpoint or the graph nodes); on any failure fall back to the existing live-fetch-first logic unchanged. If a clean backend articles-list endpoint is not warranted for Step 1, keep /api/news on its current path and document that only /api/graph is backend-backed for now — but the BACKEND_URL branch must not break the existing flow.

Update root .env.example to add: BACKEND_URL (unset by default = use built-in live fetch), NEO4J_URI, NEO4J_USER, NEO4J_PASSWORD, QDRANT_URL, QDRANT_API_KEY, DATABASE_URL, with comments explaining each and that the frontend only needs BACKEND_URL. Do NOT modify .env.local.

Write backend/README.md: (1) Local dev: uv sync, docker compose up (neo4j/qdrant/postgres/redis), alembic upgrade head, run backfill, run uvicorn + celery worker/beat. (2) How to run the backfill. (3) Env var reference. (4) Prod deploy notes: Neo4j Aura connection string form, Qdrant Cloud URL+API key, Postgres managed instance, deploying the FastAPI+Celery container to Railway/Render/Fly.io, and setting BACKEND_URL on the Vercel project to point the Next.js app at the deployed backend. (5) A clear 'verified in sandbox vs. requires managed cloud instances' section.
Add a short note to the root README.md pointing to backend/README.md for the graph/vector backbone (Step 1).
acceptance_criteria: With BACKEND_URL unset, `bun run build` and `bun run lint` behave exactly as before (baseline had only pre-existing warnings in NetworkGraph.tsx); no new errors introduced.
app/api/graph/route.ts and app/api/news/route.ts try the backend only when BACKEND_URL is set and always fall back cleanly on error/empty, never throwing to the client.
lib/backend-client.ts never throws to callers and enforces a request timeout.
Root .env.example contains BACKEND_URL, NEO4J_URI, NEO4J_USER, NEO4J_PASSWORD, QDRANT_URL, QDRANT_API_KEY, DATABASE_URL; .env.local is untouched and uncommitted.
backend/README.md documents local dev, backfill, prod deploy (Aura/Qdrant Cloud/Railway-Render-Fly), and the sandbox-verified vs. cloud-required split.
verification: cd /projects/sandbox/quant-feed- && export PATH="$HOME/.local/share/mise/shims:$PATH" && bun run lint && bun run build
findings: WHAT WAS BUILT (frontend + docs, no backend code changed except README): - lib/backend-client.ts: tiny typed client. isBackendEnabled() returns true iff process.env.BACKEND_URL is set (non-empty after trim). backendBaseUrl() trims trailing slashes. safeGetJson() does fetch with an AbortController timeout (BACKEND_TIMEOUT_MS=4000, cache:'no-store', Accept:application/json), returns null on !res.ok / thrown error / bad JSON, and clears the timer in finally. NEVER throws to callers. fetchGraphFromBackend(params) builds URLSearchParams from category (skipped when 'all'), startDate, endDate, sentiment, entity and GETs {BACKEND_URL}/graph/query. fetchArticleFromBackend(id) GETs {BACKEND_URL}/articles/{encoded id}. Exports BackendGraphResponse (extends GraphData with correlations/dataSource) and BackendArticleResponse matching the FEAT-003 contract. - app/api/graph/route.ts: hoisted categoryPlaceholders to module scope and extracted enrichNodes(nodes, articleMap) so the SAME freshnessScore + url + imageUrl enrichment is applied to both the proxied and live paths (backend does not add freshnessScore/imageUrl, per FEAT-003). Added a branch at the TOP of GET: if isBackendEnabled(), try fetchGraphFromBackend with the same category/startDate/endDate (+sentiment/entity) params; if it returns a non-empty graph, enrich nodes (empty article map -> node.freshnessScore fallback + placeholder imageUrl by category) and return { ...nodes/links, correlations, dataSource } with the existing no-store headers. On null/empty/thrown, falls through to the EXISTING live-fetch-first -> /tmp -> mock logic ENTIRELY UNCHANGED. The old inline enrichment block was replaced with a call to enrichNodes (behavior identical). With BACKEND_URL unset, isBackendEnabled() is false so the branch is skipped and behavior is exactly as before. - app/api/news/route.ts: NOT proxied (documented). Added a comment block explaining that the Step 1 backend exposes only /graph/query, /articles/{id}, /health (no articles-list endpoint), so a BACKEND_URL branch is not warranted here yet; the route keeps its live-fetch-first behavior unchanged. No functional change. - .env.example (root): added BACKEND_URL (unset by default = built-in live fetch; the ONLY var the frontend needs) plus a backend-reference block NEO4J_URI/NEO4J_USER/NEO4J_PASSWORD (with Aura form note), QDRANT_URL/QDRANT_API_KEY (Qdrant Cloud note), DATABASE_URL (SQLAlchemy URL), each commented. .env.local was NOT touched. - backend/README.md: replaced the FEAT-001 placeholder with full docs: endpoint table, requirements, local dev (uv sync, docker compose up neo4j/qdrant/postgres/redis, alembic upgrade head, neo4j schema init, python -m scripts.backfill, uvicorn, celery worker+beat with the real -A app.tasks.celery_app.celery_app target), backfill section, env var reference table, prod deploy (Neo4j Aura neo4j+s:// form, Qdrant Cloud URL+key, managed Postgres + alembic release step, managed Redis, deploying the FastAPI+Celery container to Railway/Render/Fly.io with web/worker/beat process commands, and setting BACKEND_URL on Vercel), and a 'Verified in sandbox vs. requires managed cloud instances' section noting the podman socket/networking limitation that blocked the live docker round-trip. - README.md (root): added a 'Backend: Graph/Vector Backbone (Step 1)' section pointing to backend/README.md and explaining the opt-in BACKEND_URL fallback behavior. VERIFIED: - Frontend (BACKEND_URL unset): `bun run lint` -> only the two PRE-EXISTING NetworkGraph.tsx warnings (useMemo deps + ), no new errors. `bun run build` -> succeeds, all 11 routes generated including /api/graph and /api/news. - `grep -c BACKEND_URL .env.example` = 2, `grep -c NEO4J_URI .env.example` = 1 (both present). - Backend (re-run to be safe, no code changed): `uv run ruff check .` clean, `uv run mypy .` clean (39 files), `uv run pytest -q` 44 passed. DID NOT TOUCH: the 3D engine / NetworkGraph rendering (Step 2). Frontend changes limited to lib/backend-client.ts, app/api/graph/route.ts, app/api/news/route.ts, root .env.example, root README.md, backend/README.md. .env.local untouched/uncommitted. MOCKED vs LIVE: the end-to-end Vercel(BACKEND_URL set)->deployed-backend proxy round-trip requires managed cloud datastores (Neo4j Aura/Qdrant Cloud/managed Postgres) or a working local Docker host; it could not be exercised in-sandbox due to the podman socket/networking limitation documented in FEAT-001/002/003. The fallback path (BACKEND_URL unset) is fully verified via build+lint and behaves exactly as before.
